title: Backcasting from Zero Successful Insider Threat Attacks: Minimum Viable Access Controls for Agent Deployments

original_idea.body:
# Backcasting from Zero Successful Insider Threat Attacks: Minimum Viable Access Controls for Agent Deployments

**Problem:** Success state: no AI agent acts as an insider threat in an organization. Working backward, what minimum access control policies prevent this without excessively limiting agent utility?

**Direction:** Model an organization's data and tool graph. Apply principle-of-least-privilege systematically. Measure what fraction of typical agent task categories can be completed under minimal access controls. Identify the access-control policies that minimize insider threat surface while preserving utility.

**Why it matters:** Access control is the first line of defense against insider threats. This study provides an evidence-based specification for agent deployment policies.

**Relevant context:** AI insider threat literature; principle-of-least-privilege; LW threat matrix.
